title: Billie Holiday and Helen Humes: who came first
summary: Clayton and Dance sort out whether Billie or Helen came first, and recall arranging 'I Can't Get Started' for Billie.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: : Yes. That's where the band really started to click?
I'd say so. And we had picked up Helen Humes.
Ah, Helen Humes now, came in the band about the same time with, but Billie wasn't too long with our band.
No, I think it was quite a short time.
She was with the band when I came here in 1937. And I think Helen must have come after.

She might have, yes. But I know Helen, yes, Billie was first. Because Billie had been with us I believe when we went to the Famous Door. We met, she came from, she came out to Pittsburgh and I made an arrangement for 'I Can't Get Started With You' for her.

One of the first things she did for Basie's band. But I do know Helen was in the Famous Door. That I know, because I've got the write-ups at home. I look at them, pictures of me and Joe Jones and Jimmy Rushing and Helen Humes and it goes on to tell about the success in the Famous Door.
Maybe Helen was in and out then?
Well, I know Billie wasn't in the Famous Door with us. She wasn't, she never did sing in the Famous Door.
Well, let's see, I was you here in March '37, and we were playing in Scranton. Because John took me there to hear the band. Billie was there then.
